What you can do with dsOMOP

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-showcase.Rmd
book-showcase.Rmd

What you will learn

See six things you can build while patient rows stay on the server, then choose the chapter that teaches your next step.

Read the cards as a quick tour, or run them in order. Each output is a real 2.10.5 result. The first four cards use the 24-person synthetic questionnaire fixture, not APHRC patient data; the last two use synthetic Synthea27Nj labs.

You need: the packages and downloaded helpers from Before you start. Start a fresh R session in book-work. The local fixture makes the vocabulary comparison reproducible.

library(dsOMOPClient)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/fixture.R")
practice <- book_fixture(two_sites = TRUE)
conns <- practice$conns
names(conns)
#> [1] "site"  "site2"

The two sites have the same synthetic answer patterns but different vocabulary wording. They illustrate harmonisation, not two independent study populations.

Named concepts across sites

One categorical column, shared meanings. Declare a common label for the same education concept, then ask each site for a protected count table.

named <- omop_recipe(variables = list(education = omop_variable(
  event = omop_event("observation", 900001L),
  reducer = omop_reduce("last_value", value = "value_as_concept_id"),
  labels = c("900102" = "University education"))),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
recipe_execute(named, out = c(people = "D_tour_named"), conns = conns)
named_tables <- lapply(names(conns), function(site)
  ds.omop.table("D_tour_named", "education", conns = conns[site]))
names(named_tables) <- names(conns)
named_tables
#> $site
#> D_tour_named$education
#>  Secondary education University education 
#>                    6                    6 
#> 
#> $site2
#> D_tour_named$education
#>  Secondary education University education 
#>                    6                    6

The same labels appear at both sites even though their local names differ. These are released counts, not an export of education answers. Learn concepts and harmonisation →

Use one site for the next three cards; keep the other connection for cleanup.

two_conns <- conns
conns <- two_conns[1L]
names(conns)
#> [1] "site"

Dates in your study’s format, and completed ages

Separate a date’s meaning from its presentation. This recipe uses a custom month-year pattern and completed birthdays at death.

dates <- omop_recipe(variables = list(
  month = omop_date("first_visit", omop_date_spec(precision = "custom",
    pattern = "%b %Y")), age = omop_age_at("death")),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
recipe_execute(dates, out = c(people = "D_tour_dates"), conns = conns)
ds.omop.table("D_tour_dates", "month", conns = conns)
#> D_tour_dates$month
#> Mar 2020 Jun 2020 Jul 2020 
#>        6        6        6
age_result <- dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_tour_dates$age", datasources = conns)
knitr::kable(book_summary(age_result))
Site Statistic Value
site 5% 33
site 10% 33
site 25% 33
site 50% 38
site 75% 43
site 90% 43
site 95% 43
site Mean 38

Complete birth/death records give ages 33 and 43. Missing dates stay missing. Exact dates, numeric periods, month/quarter/year categories, date parts and supported custom patterns serve different questions; category release rules still apply. Learn dates and ages →

Choose the output shape

Person → event → period → follow-up. Wide tables support named covariates; long tables retain events; panels repeat time bins; survival records end at an outcome or declared censor. All four remain private server tables.

visits <- omop_event("visit_occurrence", c(9201L, 9202L), name = "visits")
visitors <- omop_population("visitors", index = omop_index(visits))
base <- omop_recipe(events = list(visits), populations = list(visitors),
  variables = list(visits = omop_variable(event = visits, reducer = omop_reduce("count"))),
  outputs = omop_output("wide", rows = "visitors", format = "wide"))
shapes <- list(
  wide = base$outputs[[1L]],
  long = omop_output("long", rows = "visitors", format = "long", sources = "visits"),
  panel = omop_output("panel", rows = "visitors", format = "person_period",
    options = list(sources = list(visits), bins = list(width = 30L),
      window = omop_window(1, 90), analyses = "count")),
  survival = omop_output("survival", rows = "visitors", format = "survival",
    options = list(outcomes = list(revisit = visits), tar = omop_window(1, 365),
      censor = list("observation_end", "death"))))

The same population enters at its first visit. The panel has three 30-day bins; survival asks about the first repeat visit within a year, stopping earlier at observation end or death.

shape_columns <- lapply(names(shapes), function(shape) {
  recipe <- base
  recipe$outputs <- setNames(list(shapes[[shape]]), shape)
  stopifnot(recipe_explain(recipe, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
  target <- paste0("D_tour_", shape)
  recipe_execute(recipe, out = setNames(target, shape), conns = conns)
  columns <- dsBaseClient::ds.colnames(target, datasources = conns)[[1L]]
  data.frame(Shape = shape, Columns = paste(columns, collapse = ", "))
})
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, shape_columns))
Shape Columns
wide row_id, cohort_row_id, person_id, visits
long row_id, cohort_row_id, person_id, concept_id, start_date, end_date, visit_type_concept_id
panel row_id, cohort_row_id, person_id, period_start_days, period_end_days, days, visits_inpatient_visit_count, visits_outpatient_visit_count
survival row_id, cohort_row_id, person_id, outcome_name, event, entry_days_from_index, exit_days_from_index, follow_up_days

These are actual released column inventories, not patient rows. Panels and long tables contain repeated observations, so row count is not independent sample size.

More shapes: presets, intervals, sparse data and joins

Features and baseline are wide presets. Temporal covariates add time indices to sparse values; intervals retain bounds; membership retains population episodes; a dictionary describes concepts; joined combines declared private dependencies. The following executes each additional form on the same small study.

more <- list(
  features = omop_output("features", rows = "visitors", type = "features"),
  baseline = omop_output("baseline", rows = "visitors", type = "baseline"),
  intervals = omop_output("intervals", rows = "visitors", format = "intervals",
    options = list(sources = list(visits), window = omop_window(0, NULL))),
  sparse = omop_output("sparse", rows = "visitors", format = "sparse",
    options = list(sources = list(visits), analyses = "count")),
  temporal = omop_output("temporal", rows = "visitors", format = "temporal_covariates",
    options = list(sources = list(visits), bin_width = 30L,
      window = omop_window(0, 89), analyses = "count")),
  membership = omop_output("membership", rows = "visitors", format = "membership"))
more_columns <- lapply(names(more), function(shape) {
  recipe <- base
  recipe$outputs <- setNames(list(more[[shape]]), shape)
  stopifnot(recipe_explain(recipe, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
  target <- paste0("D_tour_", shape)
  recipe_execute(recipe, out = setNames(target, shape), conns = conns)
  data.frame(Shape = shape, Columns = paste(
    dsBaseClient::ds.colnames(target, datasources = conns)[[1L]], collapse = ", "))
})
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, more_columns))
Shape Columns
features row_id, cohort_row_id, person_id, visits
baseline row_id, cohort_row_id, person_id, visits
intervals row_id, cohort_row_id, person_id, interval_type, concept_id, start_days_from_index, end_days_from_index
sparse row_id, cohort_row_id, person_id, covariate_id, covariate_value
temporal row_id, cohort_row_id, person_id, time_id, covariate_id, covariate_value
membership row_id, cohort_row_id, person_id, cohort_start_date, cohort_end_date, index_source

Sparse outputs also create reference companions that define their numeric keys. Keep those companions for interpretation.

dictionary <- base
dictionary$outputs$dictionary <- omop_output("dictionary", rows = "visitors",
  format = "dictionary", options = list(source_outputs = "wide"))
dictionary$publish <- "dictionary"
recipe_execute(dictionary, out = c(dictionary = "D_tour_dictionary"), conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.colnames("D_tour_dictionary", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> [1] "concept_id"       "concept_name"     "domain_id"        "vocabulary_id"   
#> [5] "concept_class_id" "source"
joined <- base
joined$variables$age <- omop_age_at("first_visit")
joined$outputs <- list(
  counts = omop_output("counts", rows = "visitors", format = "wide", columns = "visits"),
  ages = omop_output("ages", rows = "visitors", format = "wide", columns = "age"),
  joined = omop_output("joined", rows = "visitors", format = "joined",
    options = list(from = list(list(output = "counts"), list(output = "ages")),
      how = "left", cardinality = "one_to_one")))
joined$publish <- "joined"
recipe_execute(joined, out = c(joined = "D_tour_joined"), conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.colnames("D_tour_joined", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> [1] "row_id"        "cohort_row_id" "person_id"     "visits"        "age"

The join adds an age column without multiplying episodes. Only the dictionary or joined result is published in those respective calls.

The APHRC colleague’s verbal-autopsy table

One wide table combines the study variables. The downloadable helper builds the released recipe: pseudonymous person key, completed ages, education and fever answers, visit periods, dates and coded cause of death.

source("tools/dates/va-native.R")
va <- va_native_recipe()
recipe_execute(va, out = c(people = "D_tour_va"), conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.colnames("D_tour_va", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#>  [1] "person_id"          "age_at_death"       "age_at_first_visit" "education"         
#>  [5] "fever"              "visit_date"         "visit_month"        "visit_quarter"     
#>  [9] "visit_year"         "visit_parts_year"   "visit_parts_month"  "death_date"        
#> [13] "cause_of_death"
ds.omop.table("D_tour_va", "cause_of_death", conns = conns)
#> D_tour_va$cause_of_death
#> Myocardial infarction             Pneumonia 
#>                    12                     6

The cause counts are synthetic questionnaire-fixture results, not APHRC findings. The person key and patient rows stay private; education and cause are each one named categorical column in the same table. Build this table step by step →

Switch to the numeric practice resource for the last two cards. The common connection file keeps its DSLite/Opal choice in one place.

ds.omop.disconnect(conns = two_conns)
DSI::datashield.logout(two_conns)
unlink(practice$path)
source("tools/book/connection.R")
source("tools/book/practice.R")
practice <- if (book_driver == "DSLite") book_practice("numeric") else book_connect("numeric")
conns <- practice$conns
names(conns)
#> [1] "site"

Numbers and their groupings

Keep the number and a declared band. Reduce hemoglobin to one mean per person, in recorded g/dL, and group those means using public teaching breaks.

labs <- omop_recipe(variables = list(hb = omop_variable(event = omop_event("measurement", 3000963L,
  unit = omop_unit(8713L)), reducer = omop_reduce("mean"))),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
recipe_execute(labs, out = c(people = "D_tour_labs"), conns = conns)
tour_mean <- labs$variables$hb
tour_mean$name <- NULL
bands <- omop_recipe(variables = list(hb = tour_mean,
  band = omop_number_bins(tour_mean, breaks = c(-Inf, 14, 15, Inf),
    labels = c("below 14", "14 to below 15", "15 or above"))))
recipe_execute(bands, out = c(output = "D_tour_bands"), conns = conns)
band_result <- dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_tour_bands$band", useNA = "no", datasources = conns)
mean_result <- dsBaseClient::ds.mean("D_tour_bands$hb", type = "combine", datasources = conns)
band_display <- book_group_comparison(band_result, mean_result, "Person mean hemoglobin", "g/dL")
band_display$Category <- ordered(band_display$Category,
  levels = c("below 14", "14 to below 15", "15 or above"))
knitr::kable(band_display[order(band_display$Category), c("Category", "Count", "Mean")],
  row.names = FALSE, col.names = c("Band (g/dL)", "People", "Mean (g/dL)"))
Band (g/dL) People Mean (g/dL)
below 14 9 14.46679
14 to below 15 9 14.46679
15 or above 10 14.46679

Counts 9, 9 and 10 cover all 28 people. The repeated numeric mean is the overall mean of person means, not a mean within each band. The factor is ordered on the server; the display follows its declared order. The breaks are teaching choices, not clinical ranges. Learn reducers, units, flags and pooled analysis →

Derive and filter without downloading rows

Present the number, then select with a condition. Native unit conversion declares the coordinate; omop_where declares the filter predicate. Standalone mutate remains useful for general derived columns in an already assigned table.

converted <- omop_recipe(variables = list(hb = tour_mean,
  hb_gl = omop_number(tour_mean, omop_number_spec(
    unit = omop_number_unit("unit:8713", "unit:8636", 10)))))
recipe_execute(converted, out = c(output = "D_tour_converted"), conns = conns)
ds.omop.filter("D_tour_converted", expr = omop_where(hb >= 14),
  newobj = "D_tour_selected", conns = conns)
selected_result <- dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_tour_selected$hb_gl", datasources = conns)
knitr::kable(book_summary(selected_result))
Site Statistic Value
site 5% 140.9333
site 10% 141.0533
site 25% 143.2500
site 50% 151.2500
site 75% 155.7917
site 90% 158.9000
site 95% 159.9500
site Mean 149.9991

The retained people’s values are expressed in g/L, ten times g/dL. The final subset passes its publication check; the analyst receives only this summary. Learn BMI, age groups, recodes and rollback →

Try it

Use the converted table to summarise all people, without the filter. Why does the mean differ from the preceding card?

Solution

all_result <- dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_tour_converted$hb_gl", datasources = conns)
knitr::kable(book_summary(all_result))
Site Statistic Value
site 5% 129.0500
site 10% 131.4667
site 25% 137.8500
site 50% 143.2500
site 75% 153.3542
site 90% 157.0000
site 95% 159.2375
site Mean 144.6679

This mean is 144.667857 g/L, ten times the earlier all-person mean in g/dL. The filtered card excludes people whose person mean is below 14 g/dL, so its mean is higher. The unit conversion alone does not select people.

Exercise 2: a common variant

Inspect the numeric card’s output schema.

Solution 2

dsBaseClient::ds.colnames("D_tour_bands", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> [1] "person_id" "hb"        "band"

The raw number and the group coexist, so a reader can choose the representation appropriate to the analysis.

Exercise 3: a pitfall to avoid

Count people by the declared haemoglobin bands.

Solution 3

knitr::kable(book_counts(dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_tour_bands$band", datasources = conns)))
Category Count
below 14 9
14 to below 15 9
15 or above 10
NA 0

The grouped result is a checked aggregate; the 28 underlying rows remain on the server.

Recap

Select concepts, choose time and units, request the table shape, and derive columns privately. DataSHIELD returns approved summaries while rows stay at sites.
